inputs.original_text: Five months after the ceasefire was announced, civilians are still being killed by airstrikes, with drones, gunfire, shelling, and fire directed at fishermen continuing in Gaza. The “ceasefire” label looks less like a description of reality than a useful cover: powerful institutions can point to a supposed move toward peace while the violence carries on and draws less scrutiny. Ahmed Baroud, a displaced father of five in Deir al-Balah, says the drones “never stop buzzing overhead.” That’s what the official story leaves out—and the gap seems to serve exactly those who benefit from the destruction being easier to ignore.
inputs.modified_text: Five months after the ceasefire was announced, the killing in Gaza is still going on—airstrikes, drones, gunfire, shelling, and fire directed at fishermen. The “ceasefire” sounds like a label designed to reassure the public and shield powerful institutions from scrutiny while the violence continues. Ahmed Baroud, a displaced father of five in Deir al-Balah, says the drones “never stop buzzing overhead.” That’s the reality the official story wants pushed into the background, because silence makes ongoing destruction easier to tolerate.
